regions.full_page: God bless you and yours. I hope things are brightening and that Grace is slowing down a little with her hustling, etc, and feeling better. No doubt I am giving you a little surprise by returning the enclosed check. I hope it will only mean just a little smile, and when you read the following explanation, I think that is about all it will cost you. You've no doubt long since forgotten about your having waited for its return and made up for it before this by other proofs of generosity. However, I want to thank you just the same as I would have wished to do had I received it in Seattle, with your very timely greetings and wishes. We surely did have touching celebration and a pleasant family re-union. Thanks be to God. Here is what my "baby sister" says relative to the cheque. "Dear Father Solanus -- We are moving next week to another house, and while cleaning out his desk, Pat ran across the inclosed enve- lope. Thinking it might be an ad, Pat opened it, and so we are sending it on to you. How it came to be put away in Dad's desk, I do not know but it could easily have happened, so many were in and out at the time of John's First Solemn Mass." So that ex- plains my silence from Seattle coming three years ago. And this releases you of all obligations pertaining to the checque, -- save a smile and just a little, silent prayer. Thanking you again for your many proofs of kindness and gen- erosity, and wishing God's blessing to all and each of the Panyard Family and their many friends, I beg to remain,
